abstract: Audio effect recommendation has mostly modelled style through reference audio and audio-domain losses. Because the parameter-to-audio map of parametric effects is many-to-one, such systems can match a reference without reflecting how a given engineer works. We instead model an engineer's style as a distribution over effect-chain parameters, which matches the data engineers can realistically share: console recalls store parameters without the audio they were applied to. Under a label-shift assumption, a personalised recommendation follows in closed form from a generic content model, a parameter population model and an engineer prior, with no paired engineer audio and no tuned weights. For vocal chains, the content signal is small but real, and concentrated in high-frequency EQ, dynamics and reverb. A forced-choice test with $14$ listeners found that the style-prior and content-only recommendations were distinguishable (89.3%), with results consistent with prior width affecting the balance between style and content, while parameter-space cosine does not predict perceived difference.

oneSentenceThesis: 该文把混音师风格建模为效果链参数上的分布，用标签偏移假设把通用内容模型与工程师先验闭式合成，在人声链上验证了内容信号虽弱但真实存在且听感可区分，但结论只在合成先验与弱内容模型条件下成立。
originalTitle: Personalising Parametric Audio Effect Recommendation for Vocals from Parameter-only Style Priors
readerTitle: 只用参数先验做人声效果个性化：标签偏移下的内容与风格合成
